claude.performance_metric: no divestiture; company remained private; Charlotte HQ closed (~320 employees affected), later relocated to Switzerland
claude.rationale: This was a whole-entity going-private merger: section 2 documents that T4 (Chiquita/Fresh Express branded produce) and T5 (farming, processing, sourcing, distribution, logistics) both transferred and continued together under new ownership, so gap_45=0 (product and its processes moved coherently). T5 operations continued with added Cutrale value-chain access while the T6 change (Charlotte HQ closure, later Switzerland relocation) was concentrated at the organization tier and, per section 4/P5, is not characterized as an operations-organization fracture disrupting production, so gap_56=0 and p5_pathway=0. Section 4/P4 documents no product-process disruption (franchises and operating capabilities retained), so p4_pathway=0. Since no structural gap was coded in B, gap_mitigated=NA.

gemini.performance_metric: No divestiture identified; the company remained privately held
gemini.rationale: The dossier indicates that the product and process tiers transferred together as part of a whole-entity acquisition, presenting no structural mismatch at closing (gap_45=0, gap_56=0). Post-deal, there is no documented disruption at the product-process interface (p4_pathway=0). Although the Charlotte headquarters was closed and the organization restructured, the sourced material explicitly notes this is not characterized as an operations-organization fracture disrupting production (p5_pathway=0).

grok.rationale: Section 2 states T4 transferred whole and T5 continued with added Cutrale capabilities (gap_45=0); T5 transferred while T6 saw HQ closure and streamlining but no documented process-organization fracture at closing (gap_56=0). Sections 3-4 explicitly code P4 and P5 as none documented at 3-5yr horizon. Section 5 confirms whole-entity merger with no transitional-services agreement required.
